description: Machine-readable rules learned from past engagements. Each subagent reads its own section at the start of every run and applies the rules at the points documented in its agent .md. Rules are appended by /retro apply; never edit by hand unless you know what you're doing — /forget will land in v1.5.

passA_timeout_floor_secs.rationale: elastic org has ~600 repos at ~24s/repo; 10-min (600s) cap covers only ~25 repos; floor at 2700s (45 min) for orgs with >200 enumerated repos

passA_timeout_floor_secs_provenance.reason: Elastic org scan timed out at 10 min covering only 250/600 repos (~42%). At ~24s/repo the full org requires ~4h. The verified find (SauceLabs credential, 12-year exposure) was in the first 250 repos; the remaining ~350 repos (elasticsearch, kibana, logstash, cloud services) were never scanned. A floor of 2700s (45 min) for large orgs prevents truncated scans on future runs.

gh_org_override.reason: 8x8-bounty slug → GH 404. The fallback path through base-name-derived orgs recovered (landed on 'jitsi') but a per-slug override makes it deterministic and avoids burning a discovery round-trip on every run.

gh_org_supplement.reason: When stem-derived GH org has fewer repos than threshold, the canonical org may use stem+suffix form (e.g. opera->operasoftware); surfacing alternatives prevents false negatives under strict 1-org cap

Pass A resolved github.com/opera (3 repos) rather than github.com/operasoftware (50+ repos) because the 1-org strict cap forced the bare-stem guess; a supplement that flags low-repo-count orgs for stem+suffix retry would have caught this.

asset_pattern_overrides.reason: Mirrors the MELI wayback brand-stem fix but on Check A. v1 has no snippet-fetch primitive so the rule is keyed by an exact pattern + heuristic gate rather than a generalized word-boundary recheck; intentionally narrow until v1.5 can express the general case.

internal_infra_override.note: internal infrastructure buckets are not web-crawled (B will never be positive) and S3 DNS is structurally generic (C will never be positive); exact literal name in program org source code is sufficient provenance

wildcard_stem_dns_override.note: enterprise-registrar + program-controlled DNS + wildcard-stem exact-match is sufficient evidence; internal-services wildcards in scope cannot be impersonated by third parties at scale
wildcard_stem_dns_override.reason: snapchat sc-core had A=neg/B=neg/C=positive with MarkMonitor registration + Route53 NS + explicit *.sc-core.net Tier A critical-severity wildcard in scope — DNS check C is positive precisely because of the enterprise-zone + program-scope combination; this rule fires only when all three C-gates are met.

in_scope_subdomain_override.match_condition: subdomain falls under any wildcard pattern in scope.in_scope[] (longest-suffix match against patterns like *.example.com or bare example.com)
in_scope_subdomain_override.note: Program-declared wildcard scope IS the ownership proof for subdomains. Any DNS record under an in-scope wildcard is the program's by zone-control. This rule short-circuits the 2-of-3 A/B/C aggregation for takeover-hunter candidates where Wayback (B) and GH code search (A) often return negative for dangling subdomains the program no longer references but still controls the parent DNS zone for.
in_scope_subdomain_override.reason: Added at takeover-hunter integration time. Subdomains under in-scope wildcards are owned by zone-control proof; without this override every takeover-hunter candidate would land at 'unknown' verdict for dangling subdomains that lack Wayback presence (typical, since the program already stopped linking them) and lack GH code-search hits (also typical, since dangling subdomains aren't actively referenced in code). High-confidence ownership case structurally — no third party can impersonate a record under the program's own DNS zone.

auto_info_filter.reason: Local filesystem paths must never appear in submitted bug-bounty reports. They leak researcher tooling internals and directory structure to the program triager, give competing researchers operational intel, can subtly bias triagers against the finding (looks like automated/scripted submission), and reveal internal classifier/rule identifiers that add nothing to the technical case.
auto_info_filter.reason_provenance: User direct policy instruction 2026-05-16, given twice: 'In the next reports do not include this local information like: Cache: memory/ownership-cache/00a486a91e889634.json. Those sort of thinks referring local paths of my system'. High confidence because explicit user policy, not inferred heuristic. The Automattic bundled report (H1 #3741482) shipped with 6 such leaks before this rule existed — exactly the failure mode this rule prevents going forward.

require_cap_refinement_when_all_caps_unk.reason: Bugcrowd dump via arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data does not carry per-target severity caps; all caps default to unknown which causes report_drafter severity min(proposed, cap) to silently downgrade every finding to medium

All 44 bc-monash-mbb assets have severity_cap=unknown due to Bugcrowd parser limitation; without this gate, any drafted report would have its severity silently capped at medium regardless of actual impact.
